This is true. It’s still striking to me how many people expect AI compute prices to fall simply because new capacity keeps coming online.

The demand side is digital. The supply side is physical.

Demand can grow almost exponentially overnight especially as models improve. Supply is constrained by GPUs, HBM, power, transformers, electricians, data centers, permitting… (and a hundred other bottlenecks).

In this market, GPU prices are ultimately driven by the value they unlock, not just by the cost of the hardware.

So for example: 

Company A uses GPUs to summarize internal emails. Great, it saves thousands of hours so millions of dollars. 

Company B uses those same GPUs to discover a new drug or make a scientific breakthrough worth tens of billions. Company B will simply outbid Company A. 

As AI expands into more frontier use cases with enormous economic value, the willingness to pay for the newest compute keeps increasing. So even as supply grows, don’t be surprised if frontier compute remains expensive, or even gets more expensive!
